patch.summary:
PATCH /stations/{station}: names, requires_overseer and sort of a station of the branch (the route binding is the branch
scope: another branch's station, or a deleted one, is a 404). The code never changes

ApproveCountRequest.description: POST /stock-counts/{count}/approve: an optional note, kept as the count's decision note.
ApproveCountRequest.title: ApproveCountRequest

AssignProductionRequest.description:
POST /production/requests/{request}/assign: the person who makes it, by id. Whether they are an active person of this branch
who holds production.fulfil at the request's station is the action's question (AssignRequest).
AssignProductionRequest.title: AssignProductionRequest

BroadcastingAuthRequest.description:
What Laravel Echo (pusher-js) sends before it joins a private channel: the socket id the transport gave the
connection ("1234.5678") and the channel name ("private-station.5"), as JSON or form-encoded.
BroadcastingAuthRequest.title: BroadcastingAuthRequest

CancelOrderRequest.description: POST /orders/{order}/cancel: an optional reason ("The customer left"), kept on the order and in its timeline.
CancelOrderRequest.title: CancelOrderRequest

CancelProductionRequest.description: POST /production/requests/{request}/cancel: an optional reason of at most 255 characters, kept on the request.
CancelProductionRequest.title: CancelProductionRequest

CancelPurchaseRequest.description: POST /purchases/{purchase}/cancel: an optional reason ("Supplier did not deliver"), kept on the purchase and in the audit row.
CancelPurchaseRequest.title: CancelPurchaseRequest

CancelShiftRequest.description: POST /shifts/{shift}/cancel: an optional reason, kept on the shift.
CancelShiftRequest.title: CancelShiftRequest

CosignCountRequest.description: POST /stock-counts/{count}/cosign: an optional note, kept in the audit row of the co-signature.
CosignCountRequest.title: CosignCountRequest

DoneBatchRequest.description:
POST /production/batches/{batch}/done: how many were made and how many were wasted, in the product base unit, as decimal strings
(never floats, ADR 0004), each zero or more with at most four decimals, the two together above zero. Whether the baker may press
Done on this batch, and whether the stock is there, are the action's questions (FinishBatch).
DoneBatchRequest.title: DoneBatchRequest

OpenAdHocShiftRequest.description:
POST /stations/{station}/shifts/open-ad-hoc: the call-in. The client UUID of the shift it may make, and optionally the person it
is opened for (the admin's; everyone else opens it for themselves).
OpenAdHocShiftRequest.title: OpenAdHocShiftRequest

PublishRecipeRequest.description:
POST /items/{item}/recipe/versions: the whole next recipe (the body of PUT /items/{item}/recipe) plus an optional change
note of at most 255 characters that says why the version was published.
PublishRecipeRequest.title: PublishRecipeRequest

PutRecipeRequest.description:
PUT /items/{item}/recipe: the whole recipe (version 1 in Phase 0): yield quantity and unit, at least one line
(a live item of the branch, each ingredient once, a positive quantity in a unit, optional flag, waste 0 <= w < 100)
and optional bilingual steps (rule 9). Quantities are decimal strings (ADR 0004). Unit convertibility and
self-reference are checked by RecipeBook against the database.
PutRecipeRequest.title: PutRecipeRequest

ReadAllRequest.description:
POST /notifications/read-all {before_id?}: with before_id only the lines up to that id are marked, so a line that arrived
after the client drew its list is not marked read unseen.
ReadAllRequest.title: ReadAllRequest

RecordPaymentRequest.description:
POST /orders/{order}/payments: the client's id for the payment (ADR 0003), the channel's code, the amount as a
decimal string (up to 10 integer digits and 2 decimals, above zero: money is never a JSON number, ADR 0004), the cash
handed over for cash, and the bank's or wallet's reference when the channel asks for one. Whether the channel is
usable, the amount is the balance and the cash covers it are Payments' rules (RecordPayment), answered with their own
message keys.
RecordPaymentRequest.title: RecordPaymentRequest

RejectCountRequest.description:
POST /stock-counts/{count}/reject: the note is required (what to look at again); `line_ids` marks the lines to look at again
(default every line with a variance; the action refuses a line that is not on the count).
RejectCountRequest.title: RejectCountRequest

RejectLineRequest.description:
POST /order-lines/{line}/reject: why the station gives the line back, one of the fixed list (RejectReason:
ingredient_spoiled, equipment_down, out_of_stock, other) and a note, which `other` needs (up to 500 characters, the
column's size; blanks are no note).
RejectLineRequest.title: RejectLineRequest

RejectTransferRequest.description:
POST /transfers/{transfer}/reject: the reason is required ("The sack is for the wedding cake"), kept on the transfer and
in the audit row, and shown to the person who asked.
RejectTransferRequest.title: RejectTransferRequest

ReplaceItemStationsRequest.description:
PUT /items/{item}/stations: the complete set of stations the item's order lines route to (an empty list makes it a
display-case item with no station step). Each a live station of the admin's branch, once.
ReplaceItemStationsRequest.title: ReplaceItemStationsRequest

ReplaceLinesRequest.description:
PUT /orders/{order}/lines: the whole list of the open cart's lines (ReadsLines); a line already on the order is
sent again under its client UUID, a line left out is removed.
ReplaceLinesRequest.title: ReplaceLinesRequest

ReplacePurchaseLinesRequest.description: PUT /purchases/{purchase}/lines: the draft's lines become exactly this list (ReadsPurchaseLines), matched by line client UUID.
ReplacePurchaseLinesRequest.title: ReplacePurchaseLinesRequest

ReplaceRosterRequest.description: PUT /shifts/{shift}/roster: the whole roster of a scheduled shift (an empty list empties it).
ReplaceRosterRequest.title: ReplaceRosterRequest

ReplaceUserStationsRequest.description: PUT /users/{id}/stations: the user's complete set of station assignments (an empty list withdraws them all).
ReplaceUserStationsRequest.title: ReplaceUserStationsRequest

ScheduleShiftRequest.description:
POST /shifts: schedule a template on a local date (Y-m-d) at a station with the people who will work it. The client UUID makes an
offline replay with a lost Idempotency-Key reach the same shift (ADR 0003). The station must be a live station of the branch (the controller refuses another with 422 validation.failed); whether the
template serves it and whether the people can work there is the action's question (ScheduleShift).
ScheduleShiftRequest.title: ScheduleShiftRequest

SendBackBatchRequest.description: POST /production/batches/{batch}/send-back: the note the baker reads on the card, required, at most 255 characters, not blank.
SendBackBatchRequest.title: SendBackBatchRequest

SetCashDeclarationRequest.description:
PUT /stock-counts/{count}/cash: `denominations` (an object, {"200": 3, ..}; always the whole count, an empty object is a drawer with
nothing in it) and any of `float_left_total`, `channels`, `reason_id`, `reason_note`. The shape is checked here; the denominations, the
sums and the channels are checked by the action, which answers 422 shifts.cash.* naming what is wrong, so a client gets the same error
whatever the mistake. A key that is absent leaves that part alone, `null` clears it. Any total sent is ignored: the server works it out.
SetCashDeclarationRequest.title: SetCashDeclarationRequest

SetCountLinesRequest.description:
PUT /stock-counts/{count}/lines: `lines` (each an `item_id` and any of `counted_qty`, `confirm`, `reason_id`, `reason_note`) and/or
`confirm_all` (the explicit "nothing changed"). The shape is checked here; a counted figure is deliberately not: the action reads
it as a decimal string or a whole JSON number and answers 422 shifts.count.qty_invalid naming the item when it is anything else,
so a client gets the same error whatever is wrong with the figure. A key that is absent leaves that field alone; `null` clears it.
SetCountLinesRequest.title: SetCountLinesRequest

SetOpeningCostRequest.description:
POST /inventory/costs/{item}/opening: the cost of the stock already on hand, per $unit_id (a decimal string with at most 4
decimals, never a float). SetOpeningCost converts it to a cost per base unit.
SetOpeningCostRequest.title: SetOpeningCostRequest

StartBatchRequest.description:
POST /production/requests/{request}/start: the client UUID of the batch (an offline replay with a lost Idempotency-Key reaches the
same batch, ADR 0003). Whether the request can be started, and by whom, is the action's question (StartBatch).
StartBatchRequest.title: StartBatchRequest

StartShiftRequest.description:
POST /stations/{station}/shifts/start: the client UUID of the shift the start may make (an offline replay with a lost
Idempotency-Key reaches the same shift, ADR 0003), optionally the scheduled instance (`shift_id`) or the template (`template_id`)
to start, `carry` (open without counting) and `force` (outside the window; the admin's,
checked by the action).
StartShiftRequest.title: StartShiftRequest

StoreCategoryRequest.description:
POST /categories: a category of one kind in the admin's branch, named in both languages (rule 9), optionally under
a live parent of the same kind and branch.
StoreCategoryRequest.title: StoreCategoryRequest

StoreDeviceRequest.description:
POST /devices: enrol a pad or till by the fingerprint it will send as X-Device-Id (globally unique, including
soft-deleted rows: a fingerprint is a physical device).
StoreDeviceRequest.title: StoreDeviceRequest

StoreDiningTableRequest.description:
POST /dining-tables: a table of the admin branch with its code (what orders snapshot as table_code; letters, digits,
dash and underscore, up to 16), both names (rule 9), optionally seats and a place in the grid. Whether the code is
free is checked by the controller (orders.table.code_taken), against inactive tables too.
StoreDiningTableRequest.title: StoreDiningTableRequest

StoreHandoverNoteRequest.description:
POST /shifts/{shift}/notes: the client UUID of the note (an offline replay writes nothing twice), its text (1 to 1000 characters in any
language, trimmed by the framework) and optionally the colleague it is for (whether they may read the station is the action's question).
StoreHandoverNoteRequest.title: StoreHandoverNoteRequest

StoreItemPriceRequest.description:
POST /items/{item}/prices: the new price as a decimal string (ADR 0004) and, optionally, when it takes effect
(ISO-8601 with an offset; default now). The currency is the branch's.
StoreItemPriceRequest.title: StoreItemPriceRequest

StoreItemRequest.description:
POST /items: an ingredient or a product of the admin's branch, named in both languages (rule 9). A product says how
it is fulfilled; an ingredient is always bought in (the default). The category holds items of the same kind; sku is
unique per branch; the batch size and the producing station belong to products only. Quantities are decimal
strings (ADR 0004).
StoreItemRequest.title: StoreItemRequest

StoreLocationRequest.description:
POST /locations: a place stock is held in, named in both languages (rule 9), of one of the location types, optionally
tied to a station of the admin's branch.
StoreLocationRequest.title: StoreLocationRequest

StoreModifierRequest.description:
POST /items/{item}/modifiers: a bilingual name (rule 9), a price delta (signed money, decimal string, default 0) and
an optional recipe delta: signed, non-zero quantities of live items of the branch, each in a unit that converts to
the item's base unit (checked by the controller against the database).
StoreModifierRequest.title: StoreModifierRequest

StoreMovementRequest.description:
POST /stock/movements: one of the Phase 0 manual movements (purchase_in, waste, return, count_adjustment) of a live
item at a live location of the admin's branch. qty is a decimal string (ADR 0004) in unit_id (default: the item's
own unit), converted to the item's base unit by the controller: a positive amount for purchase_in, return and waste
(waste is recorded as stock leaving), a signed one for count_adjustment. client_uuid makes an offline replay safe
(ADR 0003); note is kept on the audit row.
StoreMovementRequest.title: StoreMovementRequest

StoreOrderRequest.description:
POST /orders: the order's client UUID (an offline replay with a lost Idempotency-Key reaches the same order, ADR
0003), dine-in or takeaway (delivery and advance exist in the schema only, phase-1 plan section 10), a dining table
for a dine-in order only, a note, whether to send at once (default true: the pad's Send; false keeps the cart open),
and the lines (ReadsLines).
StoreOrderRequest.title: StoreOrderRequest

StoreProductionRequest.description:
POST /production/requests: ask for a to-stock product to be made. The request's client UUID (an offline replay with a lost
Idempotency-Key reaches the same request, ADR 0003), the product, how many in its base unit as a positive decimal string with
at most 4 decimals (never a float, ADR 0004; default: the product batch size), a due time and a priority (the planner's: the
action refuses them without production.plan) and a note. Whether the product is one production makes is the action's
question (CreateRequest).
StoreProductionRequest.title: StoreProductionRequest

StorePurchaseRequest.description:
POST /purchases: a draft purchase. The purchase's client UUID (an offline replay with a lost Idempotency-Key reaches the
same purchase, ADR 0003), the supplier, the invoice number (optional), the invoice date (the branch's local date), where
the goods are received (default: the branch store), notes, whether a repeated supplier + invoice number is intended, and
the lines (ReadsPurchaseLines). Whether the supplier and location are live in this branch is the action's question.
StorePurchaseRequest.title: StorePurchaseRequest

StoreReorderRuleRequest.description:
POST /reorder-rules: when an item is running low and how much to order. min_qty and reorder_qty are decimal strings in the
item's base unit (never a float, ADR 0004): the minimum may be zero, the quantity to reorder must be above zero.
location_id left out or null covers the whole branch. notify_roles left out is the default (admin and manager). Whether
the item and the place are live in this branch, whether every role exists and whether the place already has a rule is the
action's question (Reorder\ReorderRules).
StoreReorderRuleRequest.title: StoreReorderRuleRequest

StoreStationRequest.description: POST /stations: one station per code per branch (Shared's stations table), named in both languages (rule 9).
StoreStationRequest.title: StoreStationRequest

StoreSupplierRequest.description:
POST /suppliers: who a purchase is bought from. The name is a proper noun, shown as typed (no _en / _am pair); phone,
TIN and notes are optional.
StoreSupplierRequest.title: StoreSupplierRequest

StoreTemplateRequest.description:
POST /shift-templates: a named window of the day on the days of the week at some stations. Times are the branch's local
wall-clock HH:MM (an end earlier than the start crosses midnight; equal times are refused by the action:
422 shifts.template.window_invalid), days are ISO weekdays 1 (Monday) to 7, stations are checked against the branch by the action
(422 shifts.template.station_unknown).
StoreTemplateRequest.title: StoreTemplateRequest

StoreTransferRequest.description:
POST /transfers: ask for stock to be moved. The transfer's client UUID (an offline replay with a lost Idempotency-Key
reaches the same transfer, ADR 0003), the item, where it goes, where it comes from (default: the branch store), how much as a
positive decimal string with at most 4 decimals in `unit_id` (default: the item's base unit; never a float, ADR 0004), a
note, and the production request it was raised from. Whether the item and the places are live in this branch, whether the
unit converts and whether the requester works at the destination is the action's question (RequestTransfer).
StoreTransferRequest.title: StoreTransferRequest

StoreUnitRequest.description:
POST /units: a global unit (every branch shares it), named in both languages (rule 9). A derived unit names a base
unit (one without a base of its own) and a positive factor as a decimal string; a base unit has factor 1.
StoreUnitRequest.title: StoreUnitRequest

StoreUserRequest.description:
POST /users: a person of the admin's branch with one role, optional direct permission overrides, an optional short
code (checked again for uniqueness by ShortCodes) and a locale.
StoreUserRequest.title: StoreUserRequest

StoreVarianceReasonRequest.description:
POST /variance-reasons: a code (lower case letters, digits, underscore and hyphen, at most 32; chosen once), both names (at most
80), whether the counter must write a note, and where it goes in the order. A code the branch already has is 409
shifts.reason.code_taken, decided by the action.
StoreVarianceReasonRequest.title: StoreVarianceReasonRequest

SubscribePushRequest.description:
POST /notifications/endpoints {driver: "push", subscription: {endpoint, keys: {p256dh, auth}}, user_agent?}: what the
browser's PushManager.subscribe() returns (its toJSON()). Only push subscribes this way; a Telegram chat is linked with a
one-time code instead (POST /notifications/telegram/link). The endpoint must be an https URL, as the Web Push protocol
requires.
SubscribePushRequest.title: SubscribePushRequest

UnlockCountRequest.description: POST /stock-counts/{count}/unlock: the reason is required (it is kept on the revision and in the audit row).
UnlockCountRequest.title: UnlockCountRequest

UpdateCategoryRequest.description:
PATCH /categories/{category}: rename (both languages stay filled, rule 9), move under another live category of the
same kind and branch, or reorder. The kind is fixed: the items it holds are of that kind.
UpdateCategoryRequest.title: UpdateCategoryRequest

UpdateDiningTableRequest.description:
PATCH /dining-tables/{table}: rename (both languages stay filled, rule 9), change the seats or the place in the grid,
or switch the table off and on (is_active). The code is fixed: orders snapshot it.
UpdateDiningTableRequest.title: UpdateDiningTableRequest

UpdateItemRequest.description:
PATCH /items/{item}: any subset of the editable attributes. The kind is fixed (it decides which inventory the
item's stock belongs to); an ingredient stays bought in; the unit may change only within the same base unit (the
controller checks, since every stock movement of the item is written in that base).

default_batch_qty.description: a batch size and a producing station belong to products only

UpdateItemRequest.title: UpdateItemRequest

UpdateLocationRequest.description:
PATCH /locations/{location}: rename it or tie it to another station (or none). The type is fixed: it decides where
availability is computed (display-case products at the display_case location), so a store never turns into one.
UpdateLocationRequest.title: UpdateLocationRequest

UpdateReorderRuleRequest.description:
PATCH /reorder-rules/{rule}: any of the minimum, the quantity to reorder, the roles to tell and the switch; a field left out
stays. The item and the place of a rule never change (a field naming them is ignored): delete the rule and make another.
UpdateReorderRuleRequest.title: UpdateReorderRuleRequest

UpdateStationRequest.description:
PATCH /stations/{station}: any subset of the names (both languages, rule 9), requires_overseer, tracks_shifts and sort. The code is fixed
once a station exists (routing, permissions and the seeders name stations by it), so sending one is refused rather than
ignored.
UpdateStationRequest.title: UpdateStationRequest

UpdateSupplierRequest.description:
PATCH /suppliers/{supplier}: any of the supplier fields; a field left out stays, null clears an optional one. A
supplier is switched off with is_active = false (a purchase can no longer be started with it); there is no delete.
UpdateSupplierRequest.title: UpdateSupplierRequest

UpdateTemplateRequest.description: PATCH /shift-templates/{template}: any of the fields of a template. Instances already made keep their own window.
UpdateTemplateRequest.title: UpdateTemplateRequest

UpdateUserRequest.description:
PATCH /users/{id}: any subset of the editable attributes, the role, and the direct permission overrides (sent as
the complete new list). Phone is not editable here: it is the login id.
UpdateUserRequest.title: UpdateUserRequest

UpdateVarianceReasonRequest.description:
PATCH /variance-reasons/{reason}: any of the names, the note rule, the switch and the order. The code never changes: a `code` in the
body is not a rule here, so validated() drops it.
UpdateVarianceReasonRequest.title: UpdateVarianceReasonRequest

UploadFileRequest.description:
POST /files (multipart/form-data): `file` (any picture; Files decides what it accepts, in its documented order), `purpose` (`receipt` or
`refund_proof`) and `client_uuid` (ADR 0003). A request with no usable file part is 422 files.missing; a part the server cut off at its
own size limit is 422 files.too_large. Everything else wrong with the fields is the ordinary validation.failed.
UploadFileRequest.title: UploadFileRequest

user_id.description: the pad may name the person whose code is typed (per-user lockout) and, before enrolment, its branch

VoidOrderRequest.description:
POST /orders/{order}/void: why (free text, required, up to 255 characters, the column's size) and the PIN of the
manager or admin who approves it (their short code: 4 to 6 digits, typed on the asker's screen). Blanks are no reason.
VoidOrderRequest.title: VoidOrderRequest

errors.description: A detailed description of each field that failed validation.
